q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of ayurvedic medicines per kg?
title: Ayurvedic medicine carbon footprint
short: Add the herbs, ghee, jaggery, honey or oils in the formulation, then decoction and drying fuel, grinding and tablet or syrup filling electricity, and the bottles and cartons. Divide by kilograms or litres packed. Boiling fuel and packaging are often the largest plant lines.

ul: Dried herbs and roots: count kilograms bought per batch.
Ghee, oils, jaggery or honey in ghritam, tailam, arishtam and lehyam forms: ghee carries a dairy footprint.
Decoction boilers or firewood furnaces: firewood CO2 is biogenic and reported separately; LPG or diesel is Scope 1.
Tablet presses, capsule fillers and bottle lines.

p: Report by dosage form: per kg of churna or tablets, per litre of arishtam or syrup. Glass bottles add a lot per litre, so state the pack.

example.title: Worked example: ayurvedic unit per kg (one month)
lines: Decoction LPG: 2,000 kg x 2.98 = 5,960 kg CO2
Plant total: 13,060 / 20,000 = 0.653 kg CO2 per kg
Add herbs, ghee or oils, and bottles for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
